# linearctl project

<!-- Generated by scripts/skill-docs.py from --help; do not edit. -->

## linearctl project list

```
List projects.

Fields: id, name, url, targetDate, status, lead

Usage:
  linearctl project list [flags]

Examples:
  linearctl project list --team ENG --status started --json

Flags:
      --cursor CURSOR   continue after CURSOR (nextCursor from the previous page)
      --fields FIELDS   return only these comma-separated FIELDS (see Fields above)
  -h, --help            help for list
      --limit N         show at most N items; 0 for all (default 50)
      --status TYPE     only projects whose status is TYPE (repeatable):
                        backlog, planned, started, paused, completed, canceled
      --team KEY        only team KEY (falls back to LINEARCTL_TEAM, then default-team)
```

## linearctl project show

```
Show a project: its description, overview (content), status, health, documents,
milestones and issues. Documents are read in full.
PROJECT is a linear.app project URL, its slugId (the hex the URL ends with), a UUID,
or its exact name.

Fields: id, name, slugId, url, description, content, status, lead, startDate,
targetDate, progress, health, createdAt, updatedAt, teams, documents,
projectMilestones, issues

Usage:
  linearctl project show PROJECT [flags]

Examples:
  linearctl project show https://linear.app/acme/project/q4-launch-0527ca4c9128
  linearctl project show "Q4 launch" --issues 100 --fields name,content,issues --json

Flags:
      --fields FIELDS   return only these comma-separated FIELDS (see Fields above)
  -h, --help            help for show
      --issues N        include the first N issues; 0 for none (default 50)
```

## linearctl project update

```
Change a project's name, description (its one-line summary) or content (the
overview document; the new text replaces all of it). Only fields that differ are
sent; when none do, nothing is sent and the result is changed: false.
PROJECT is a URL, slugId, UUID or exact name, as for project show.
Changes things: pass --dry-run to preview, --yes to apply.

Usage:
  linearctl project update PROJECT [flags]

Examples:
  linearctl project update "Q4 launch" --content-file overview.md --dry-run --json
  linearctl project update 0527ca4c9128 --description "Ship the new login" --yes

Flags:
      --content TEXT            the new overview, Markdown TEXT; replaces all of it
      --content-file PATH       read the overview from PATH (- for stdin)
      --description TEXT        the new one-line summary, TEXT
      --description-file PATH   read the summary from PATH (- for stdin)
      --dry-run                 show what would change; change nothing
  -h, --help                    help for update
      --name TEXT               the new name, TEXT
      --yes                     apply the change
```
